groups.label: AWS CLOUD · account A unless stated
GLOBAL / EDGE · outside regional VPC boundaries
REGIONAL AWS SERVICES · outside your VPC
REGIONAL DELIVERY / OPERATIONS · control plane, not user traffic

nodes.label: Clients / devices
nodes.placement: Outside AWS: caller device, application or corporate/external identity system.
nodes.description: Browser, mobile app, SDK or telemetry producer.
nodes.flow: Creates requests/events → authenticates or signs where required → receives responses.
nodes.retention: The client owns local state. A successful transport response is separate from durable application completion.
nodes.trap: Different scenarios are alternatives; no client must traverse every service.
nodes.networkRequirements: External identity/network requirements belong to the calling system.

nodes.label: Corporate / OIDC IdP
nodes.placement: Outside AWS: caller device, application or corporate/external identity system.
nodes.description: Authenticates an external principal and issues trusted assertions.
nodes.flow: Credentials → authentication → OIDC/SAML assertion.
nodes.retention: Provider-managed identity/session state; assertion expiry and trust configuration determine accepted access.
nodes.trap: A JWT alone is not an IAM permission or an AWS access key.
nodes.networkRequirements: External identity/network requirements belong to the calling system.

nodes.label: Route 53
nodes.placement: Outside the Region/VPC boundary. This is a global or edge-scoped service/control.
nodes.description: Answers DNS queries with the configured record/routing policy.
nodes.flow: DNS query → address/alias response; HTTP travels to the resolved destination.
nodes.retention: DNS records persist as configuration; resolvers cache answers according to TTL. This is not application-message storage.
nodes.trap: DNS is not an HTTP proxy and is not a packet hop in the request path.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: CloudFront
nodes.placement: Outside the Region/VPC boundary. This is a global or edge-scoped service/control.
nodes.description: Caches and delivers content from edge locations.
nodes.flow: Viewer HTTP request → edge cache / configured origin → response.
nodes.retention: Cached responses live according to cache policies/TTL and invalidation; the origin remains a separate system.
nodes.trap: An origin can be an ALB, S3 or API; they are alternatives, not a required chain.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: IAM roles / policies
nodes.placement: Outside the Region/VPC boundary. This is a global or edge-scoped service/control.
nodes.description: Establish AWS trust and evaluate permissions.
nodes.flow: Principal + action + resource + context → policy evaluation → allow/deny.
nodes.retention: Identity, trust and permission configuration persists; it does not store application request data.
nodes.trap: Trust allows role assumption; permission policies authorize later actions. Explicit denies and applicable guardrails still apply.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Organizations / SCP
nodes.placement: Outside the Region/VPC boundary. This is a global or edge-scoped service/control.
nodes.description: Apply account-level organizational permission guardrails.
nodes.flow: Applicable organization controls → restrict available IAM permissions.
nodes.retention: Organization/account policy configuration persists. An SCP is a guardrail, not a resource that consumes jobs.
nodes.trap: An SCP does not grant permissions; evaluate exceptions and policy applicability.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: WAF · edge ACL
nodes.placement: Outside the Region/VPC boundary. This is a global or edge-scoped service/control.
nodes.description: Evaluate web requests using an associated CloudFront web ACL.
nodes.flow: CloudFront request inspection → allow/block/challenge decision.
nodes.retention: Rules persist; request logging is separately configured. Allow/block decisions do not provide durable business state.
nodes.trap: WAF is an associated inspection policy, not an extra network proxy.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: AWS Budgets
nodes.placement: Outside the Region/VPC boundary. This is a global or edge-scoped service/control.
nodes.description: Track spend/usage against configured budgets.
nodes.flow: Billing measurements → budget evaluation → configured notifications/actions.
nodes.retention: Budget definitions and billing measurements support cost tracking, not application job retention.
nodes.trap: Budget alerts are not a hard real-time spending cap.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Cross-account role
nodes.placement: IAM role in a different AWS account; a logical identity, not a network hop.
nodes.description: A role in account B trusted by an authorized principal from account A.
nodes.flow: STS request → trust validation → temporary role credentials.
nodes.retention: Role configuration persists; issued sessions expire. Assuming a role does not copy application data.
nodes.trap: Both sides must allow the relationship. The role session is still restricted by applicable policies.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Auto Scaling group
nodes.placement: Associated with the VPC; not an application server or a subnet-hosted service.
nodes.description: Maintain fleet capacity across AZs; pair with ELB to route traffic.
nodes.flow: Route/control association → relevant destinations.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Routes, filtering and service permissions must each allow the intended operation.
nodes.networkRequirements: The ASG selects subnets and a launch template; security groups apply to launched instance ENIs, not an ASG network endpoint.

nodes.label: Internet Gateway
nodes.placement: Associated with the VPC; not an application server or a subnet-hosted service.
nodes.description: VPC-attached internet gateway for appropriately routed public resources.
nodes.flow: Route/control association → relevant destinations.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Routes, filtering and service permissions must each allow the intended operation.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC/route association, not a subnet-hosted appliance with its own security group. Check the required routes and endpoint/resource policies.

nodes.label: Gateway endpoint
nodes.placement: Associated with the VPC; not an application server or a subnet-hosted service.
nodes.description: Route-table destination for private S3/DynamoDB service access.
nodes.flow: Route/control association → relevant destinations.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Routes, filtering and service permissions must each allow the intended operation.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC/route association, not a subnet-hosted appliance with its own security group. Check the required routes and endpoint/resource policies.

nodes.label: VPC peering
nodes.placement: Associated with the VPC; not an application server or a subnet-hosted service.
nodes.description: Private connectivity to a non-overlapping peer VPC.
nodes.flow: Route/control association → relevant destinations.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Routes, filtering and service permissions must each allow the intended operation.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC/route association, not a subnet-hosted appliance with its own security group. Check the required routes and endpoint/resource policies.

nodes.label: ALB node A
nodes.placement: Inside a public subnet in AZ A; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Subnet node of one regional internet-facing ALB.
nodes.flow: Client connection → listener/rule → healthy registered target.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Public ALB nodes can route to private targets. Cross-zone changes routing, not instance count.
nodes.networkRequirements: ALB uses subnets in at least two AZs and attached security groups. The two boxes are nodes of one regional ALB.

nodes.label: NAT Gateway A
nodes.placement: Inside a public subnet in AZ A; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Public NAT gateway for outbound IPv4 connections from private subnets.
nodes.flow: Private outbound connection → NAT → IGW → internet; return traffic follows connection state.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: NAT does not accept unsolicited inbound client connections. Public NAT belongs in a public subnet.
nodes.networkRequirements: Requires a subnet; public NAT also uses an Elastic IP and IGW route. NAT gateways do not support security groups; subnet NACLs still apply.

nodes.label: ALB node B
nodes.placement: Inside a public subnet in AZ B; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Subnet node of one regional internet-facing ALB.
nodes.flow: Client connection → listener/rule → healthy registered target.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Public ALB nodes can route to private targets. Cross-zone changes routing, not instance count.
nodes.networkRequirements: ALB uses subnets in at least two AZs and attached security groups. The two boxes are nodes of one regional ALB.

nodes.label: NAT Gateway B
nodes.placement: Inside a public subnet in AZ B; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Public NAT gateway for outbound IPv4 connections from private subnets.
nodes.flow: Private outbound connection → NAT → IGW → internet; return traffic follows connection state.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: NAT does not accept unsolicited inbound client connections. Public NAT belongs in a public subnet.
nodes.networkRequirements: Requires a subnet; public NAT also uses an Elastic IP and IGW route. NAT gateways do not support security groups; subnet NACLs still apply.

nodes.label: NLB node C
nodes.placement: Inside a public subnet in AZ C; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Layer-4 load-balancer node for TCP/UDP/TLS routing.
nodes.flow: Client connection → listener/rule → healthy registered target.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: NLB is Layer 4; ALB handles HTTP routing. Cross-zone defaults differ.
nodes.networkRequirements: Select subnets/AZs for NLB nodes. Security-group association is an optional creation-time choice; target controls still apply.

nodes.label: NAT Gateway C
nodes.placement: Inside a public subnet in AZ C; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Public NAT gateway for outbound IPv4 connections from private subnets.
nodes.flow: Private outbound connection → NAT → IGW → internet; return traffic follows connection state.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: NAT does not accept unsolicited inbound client connections. Public NAT belongs in a public subnet.
nodes.networkRequirements: Requires a subnet; public NAT also uses an Elastic IP and IGW route. NAT gateways do not support security groups; subnet NACLs still apply.

nodes.label: EC2 application A
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ A; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: A virtual machine with OS and instance-level control.
nodes.flow: HTTP request → application code → database/cache/API call → response.
nodes.retention: OS/process state follows the instance. Instance store is ephemeral; EBS volumes have a separately controlled lifecycle.
nodes.trap: Hardware isolation alone points to Dedicated Instances; physical host placement or socket/core licensing points to Dedicated Hosts.
nodes.networkRequirements: Requires subnet placement and ENI security groups in this VPC model; IAM instance/task permissions are independent.

nodes.label: EBS volume A
nodes.placement: AZ-scoped volume outside the subnet box. It attaches to same-AZ EC2; the volume itself has no subnet IP or security group.
nodes.description: AZ-scoped durable block storage attached to EC2 in the same AZ.
nodes.flow: EC2 block I/O ↔ volume. This is an attachment, not HTTP traffic.
nodes.retention: Independent volume lifecycle; termination deletion depends on attachment settings.
nodes.trap: No cross-AZ volume attachment. Supported Multi-Attach remains within one AZ and needs an appropriate application/filesystem.
nodes.networkRequirements: No subnet, ENI or security group. Attach to a compatible EC2 instance in the same AZ.

nodes.label: RDS primary
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ A; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Writer for this traditional Multi-AZ DB instance deployment.
nodes.flow: SQL writes/reads → primary; replicated state supports failover.
nodes.retention: Durable relational state and configured backups. Reading does not remove rows.
nodes.trap: This traditional standby is not a read endpoint. Multi-AZ DB clusters are a different model with readable standby instances.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC subnet-group/subnet placement and appropriate security groups are required for the depicted database/cache nodes.

nodes.label: EFS mount target A
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ A; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Subnet ENI exposing a regional EFS filesystem over NFS.
nodes.flow: NFS client → same-AZ mount target → shared regional filesystem.
nodes.retention: Shared filesystem persists independently of individual clients/tasks.
nodes.trap: Mount targets are endpoints; the regional filesystem is not stored inside this subnet.
nodes.networkRequirements: Mount-target ENI in the chosen subnet; mount-target security group permits the intended NFS clients.

nodes.label: Routes / SG / NACL
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ A; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Route-table and filtering annotations for this private subnet and its ENIs.
nodes.flow: Route decides destination; SG/NACL independently evaluate permitted traffic.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: SGs attach to ENIs; NACLs associate with subnets. They are controls, not chained proxy servers.
nodes.networkRequirements: Route table associates with the subnet; NACL associates with the subnet; security groups apply to the instance/task ENIs.

nodes.label: EC2 application B
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ B; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: A virtual machine with OS and instance-level control.
nodes.flow: HTTP request → application code → database/cache/API call → response.
nodes.retention: OS/process state follows the instance. Instance store is ephemeral; EBS volumes have a separately controlled lifecycle.
nodes.trap: Hardware isolation alone points to Dedicated Instances; physical host placement or socket/core licensing points to Dedicated Hosts.
nodes.networkRequirements: Requires subnet placement and ENI security groups in this VPC model; IAM instance/task permissions are independent.

nodes.label: EBS volume B
nodes.placement: AZ-scoped volume outside the subnet box. It attaches to same-AZ EC2; the volume itself has no subnet IP or security group.
nodes.description: AZ-scoped durable block storage attached to EC2 in the same AZ.
nodes.flow: EC2 block I/O ↔ volume. This is an attachment, not HTTP traffic.
nodes.retention: Independent volume lifecycle; termination deletion depends on attachment settings.
nodes.trap: No cross-AZ volume attachment. Supported Multi-Attach remains within one AZ and needs an appropriate application/filesystem.
nodes.networkRequirements: No subnet, ENI or security group. Attach to a compatible EC2 instance in the same AZ.

nodes.label: RDS standby
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ B; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Synchronous standby for availability in this traditional Multi-AZ DB instance example.
nodes.flow: SQL writes/reads → primary; replicated state supports failover.
nodes.retention: Replicated durable database state for managed promotion; traditional standby does not accept normal read queries.
nodes.trap: This traditional standby is not a read endpoint. Multi-AZ DB clusters are a different model with readable standby instances.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC subnet-group/subnet placement and appropriate security groups are required for the depicted database/cache nodes.

nodes.label: EFS mount target B
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ B; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Subnet ENI exposing a regional EFS filesystem over NFS.
nodes.flow: NFS client → same-AZ mount target → shared regional filesystem.
nodes.retention: Shared filesystem persists independently of individual clients/tasks.
nodes.trap: Mount targets are endpoints; the regional filesystem is not stored inside this subnet.
nodes.networkRequirements: Mount-target ENI in the chosen subnet; mount-target security group permits the intended NFS clients.

nodes.label: Routes / SG / NACL
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ B; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Route-table and filtering annotations for this private subnet and its ENIs.
nodes.flow: Route decides destination; SG/NACL independently evaluate permitted traffic.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: SGs attach to ENIs; NACLs associate with subnets. They are controls, not chained proxy servers.
nodes.networkRequirements: Route table associates with the subnet; NACL associates with the subnet; security groups apply to the instance/task ENIs.

nodes.label: Fargate task
nodes.scope: Task placed in one subnet / AZ
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ C; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Supply managed compute capacity for containers without managing EC2 hosts.
nodes.flow: ECS launches task → application processes requests/jobs → downstream resources.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Fargate is container compute; ECS is orchestration. Fargate does not build images or define infrastructure templates. Choose self-managed EC2 capacity when host-level requirements demand it.
nodes.networkRequirements: Requires subnet placement and ENI security groups in this VPC model; IAM instance/task permissions are independent.

nodes.label: ElastiCache
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ C; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Keep frequently reused data in memory.
nodes.flow: Cache lookup → hit returns value; miss requires authoritative-store read.
nodes.retention: Cache values expire/are evicted according to engine/settings. Persistence/replication features differ by engine; Memcached is not a durable primary store.
nodes.trap: A cache does not replace SQL access. Memcached is not a durable primary datastore.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC subnet-group/subnet placement and appropriate security groups are required for the depicted database/cache nodes.

nodes.label: RDS read replica
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ C; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Managed relational databases with SQL and transactions.
nodes.flow: Primary changes → asynchronous replica; application explicitly routes eligible reads.
nodes.retention: Asynchronously replicated persistent database state. Application reads do not delete records.
nodes.trap: Replication lag is possible. Read scaling and high-availability standby are different requirements.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC subnet-group/subnet placement and appropriate security groups are required for the depicted database/cache nodes.

nodes.label: Interface endpoint
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ C; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: PrivateLink endpoint ENI in the selected subnet.
nodes.flow: Private client → endpoint ENI → supported regional service.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: An endpoint changes connectivity, not IAM entitlement. A gateway endpoint is a different route-table mechanism.
nodes.networkRequirements: PrivateLink endpoint ENIs use selected subnets and endpoint security groups; endpoint/service policies remain separate.

nodes.label: Lambda VPC ENI
nodes.placement: Inside a private subnet in AZ C; regional service control planes are separate.
nodes.description: Optional Hyperplane ENI for Lambda access to customer VPC resources.
nodes.flow: Lambda service → managed VPC connectivity → private RDS/cache.
nodes.retention: Depends on the resource/configuration; see the full service reference.
nodes.trap: Lambda execution remains in a service-managed VPC. A public subnet does not give the function a public IP.
nodes.networkRequirements: Optional Lambda VPC configuration selects subnets and security groups; it does not move execution into a customer subnet.

nodes.label: API Gateway
nodes.placement: Regional API Gateway endpoint outside the customer VPC in this example. REST APIs also have private/edge-optimized options.
nodes.description: Expose an API with routing, integration and access controls.
nodes.flow: HTTPS request → method authorization/validation/integration → backend.
nodes.retention: API definitions/stages persist; optional REST response caches have TTLs. An accepted request need not mean asynchronous work completed.
nodes.trap: Regional endpoint in this map. REST edge-optimized/private endpoint options differ; a stage points to a deployment.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Cognito user pool
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: User directory and authentication/federation for application sign-in.
nodes.flow: Sign-in or supported federation → ID/access/refresh tokens → application/API token validation.
nodes.retention: User-directory/configuration state persists; tokens expire. An identity pool is a separate optional AWS-credential path.
nodes.trap: User pools authenticate; identity pools broker AWS credentials. Tokens do not automatically grant IAM actions.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: STS endpoint
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Issue temporary AWS session credentials after validating a supported role-assumption or federation request.
nodes.flow: Authorized role-assumption/federation request → validation → temporary credentials.
nodes.retention: STS issues expiring session credentials, not permanent access keys or durable application records.
nodes.trap: This shows a regional STS endpoint. Role trust and session permissions are separate.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: ACM certificate
nodes.placement: Regional certificates for ALB/API integrations; CloudFront viewer certificate requirement is us-east-1.
nodes.description: Provision and manage TLS certificates for supported AWS integrations.
nodes.flow: Certificate issuance/validation → attachment to supported TLS endpoint.
nodes.retention: Certificate/key metadata persists under its certificate lifecycle; it does not retain application payloads.
nodes.trap: Certificate region depends on the integration; CloudFront viewer certificates use us-east-1.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Lambda handler
nodes.placement: Lambda regional service-managed execution; optional customer-VPC connectivity is represented by the separate ENI.
nodes.description: Execute event-driven code without operating a conventional server fleet.
nodes.flow: Invocation event → application code → result/downstream AWS calls.
nodes.retention: Function code/configuration persists; an execution environment can be reused but is not a durable state store. Put durable outcomes in a data service.
nodes.trap: A JWT caller is distinct from the Lambda execution role. SAM defines the function; Lambda executes it.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Lambda alias / v1,v2
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Provide a stable named reference and optional weighted route to published Lambda versions.
nodes.flow: Alias invocation → selected published version → execution.
nodes.retention: An alias persists as routing configuration to published versions; it is not a queue or data store.
nodes.trap: Alias weights are probabilistic. A version alone does not split traffic; aliases cannot point to aliases.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Lambda worker
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Execute event-driven code without operating a conventional server fleet.
nodes.flow: Event-source batch → processing → durable result → successful batch outcome.
nodes.retention: Record the business outcome durably before acknowledging work; execution environment reuse does not guarantee persistence.
nodes.trap: At-least-once processing can repeat side effects. Record business outcomes idempotently.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Event source mapping
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Read supported event sources, batch records/messages and invoke Lambda with source-specific progress/acknowledgement behavior.
nodes.flow: Poll/subscribe to source → batch → synchronous Lambda invocation → checkpoint/acknowledgement.
nodes.retention: The integration manages source progress/acknowledgement according to source and batch outcome; it is not another application database.
nodes.trap: The event source mapping reads streams/queues; these sources do not send arbitrary HTTP requests to your handler.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: DynamoDB
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Key-value/document storage organized around key-based access.
nodes.flow: Key-based request → item/index operation → response; streams optionally record changes.
nodes.retention: Durable items remain until explicit deletion or asynchronous TTL cleanup. Application reads do not consume/delete items.
nodes.trap: TTL cleanup is asynchronous. Enforce application expiry; conditional writes prevent read-before-write races.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: DynamoDB GSI / LSI
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Maintain an alternative DynamoDB query index; GSI and LSI have different key, capacity and consistency rules.
nodes.flow: Table writes → maintained index → alternative query pattern.
nodes.retention: Maintained index projection of table data; reads do not consume the index entry. GSI propagation is eventually consistent.
nodes.trap: GSI capacity/consistency differs from the base table. LSI shares its partition key and is created with the table.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: DynamoDB Streams
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Capture a time-bounded log of DynamoDB item changes for downstream consumers.
nodes.flow: Table mutation → change record → event-source mapping → processor.
nodes.retention: A time-bounded retained change log; processing records does not delete the source table item.
nodes.trap: A stream is a change log, not a second table. Reads do not acknowledge/delete the table item.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: DAX
nodes.placement: DAX cluster nodes use customer VPC subnets and security groups; shown in the AZ C private subnet slice.
nodes.description: Accelerate supported DynamoDB operations with a VPC-based managed in-memory cluster.
nodes.flow: Supported DynamoDB client lookup → cache hit/miss → table.
nodes.retention: Cached DynamoDB values are evictable and TTL controlled; DynamoDB remains the authoritative table.
nodes.trap: DAX cluster nodes live inside VPC subnets. DAX accelerates supported DynamoDB access; it does not replace the authoritative table.
nodes.networkRequirements: VPC subnet-group/subnet placement and appropriate security groups are required for the depicted database/cache nodes.

nodes.label: SQS queue
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Buffer work so consumers can process it independently.
nodes.flow: SendMessage → retained message → ReceiveMessage → processing → DeleteMessage.
nodes.retention: SQS: retained until deletion or expiry; receive only changes visibility.
nodes.trap: Receiving hides a message temporarily; it does not delete it. FIFO does not remove all duplicate-processing risks.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: SQS dead-letter queue
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Retain repeatedly unsuccessful jobs in a separate SQS queue for investigation or redrive.
nodes.flow: Repeated unsuccessful receives → configured dead-letter queue → investigation/redrive.
nodes.retention: SQS: retained until deletion or expiry; receive only changes visibility.
nodes.trap: A DLQ is a separate queue, not an archive of all successful messages.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: SNS topic
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Publish a message to matching subscribers, including independent SQS queues.
nodes.flow: Published message → each matching subscribed destination.
nodes.retention: This models standard topic delivery/retries, not a Kinesis-style retained consumer-offset log. Supported topic archive options are a separate configuration.
nodes.trap: SNS fanout is not the same as a replayable Kinesis log.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: EventBridge bus
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Route events from an event bus to targets using rule patterns.
nodes.flow: PutEvents → matching rules → configured targets.
nodes.retention: A bus routes events; it is not the worker backlog. Configure an archive separately if replay is needed.
nodes.trap: An event bus routes events; a queue retains waiting work. They can cooperate.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Kinesis stream
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Retain continuous events in shard lanes for independent, replayable reads.
nodes.flow: Producer PutRecord(s) → hash partition key → shard → independently readable record.
nodes.retention: Kinesis: retained until configured retention expires, independently of readers.
nodes.trap: Records flow continuously; shards are capacity lanes, not delivered batches.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Kinesis shard
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Provide one ordered record lane and unit of read/write capacity inside a Kinesis stream.
nodes.flow: Append record → assigned sequence number → consumer reads retained records.
nodes.retention: Kinesis: retained until configured retention expires, independently of readers.
nodes.trap: A hot partition key maps to one shard at a time. Reads do not delete records.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: Amazon S3
nodes.placement: AWS-managed regional service, outside customer subnets. Reachability and IAM authorization are separate.
nodes.description: Store durable objects and versions accessed through authorized object APIs.
nodes.flow: Object API request → object/version operation → response or configured event.
nodes.retention: Durable object/item/filesystem state follows its own lifecycle.
nodes.trap: S3 is regional and outside customer VPCs. Presigned URLs delegate a bounded signed operation.
nodes.networkRequirements: No customer subnet or security group is required for the managed endpoint/control shown; optional integration models can change the client path.

nodes.label: EFS regional filesystem
nodes.placement: Regional filesystem outside subnet boxes; mount-target ENIs are inside selected customer subnets.
nodes.description: Provide a regional persistent shared filesystem exposed over NFS through subnet mount targets.
nodes.flow: NFS through mount targets → common filesystem → persistent files.
nodes.retention: Persistent shared regional files remain independently of client/task replacement.
nodes.trap: This is regional EFS, not EFS One Zone. Mount targets, routes and permissions still matter.
nodes.networkRequirements: The filesystem is regional; subnet ENIs/security groups belong to its mount targets shown separately.

nodes.trap: ECS orchestrates. EC2 or Fargate supplies compute; ECR stores the image.

relationships.label: TCP/UDP target routing
relationships.description: NLB selects a healthy registered target; task networking and listener protocol must match.

scenarios.title: 1 · HA web application across AZs

steps.text: Resolve the application name. Route 53 answers DNS; it does not forward HTTP.
Send HTTPS to CloudFront. A cached response can avoid the origin.
The associated WAF web ACL evaluates requests; it is not a separate proxy hop.
On an origin request, CloudFront calls the internet-facing ALB.
ALB routes to a healthy private EC2 target in AZ A.
With cross-zone routing, the same ALB node can select an enabled target in AZ B.
The application connects to the RDS writer endpoint.
The traditional Multi-AZ standby supports failover, not read scaling.

scenarios.note: Illustrative architecture: clients may use ALB directly, and CloudFront can use different origins. AZ C illustrates additional alternatives.
scenarios.exam: Availability needs redundancy and healthy capacity; adding DNS, cache or WAF is a separate requirement.

scenarios.title: 2 · Public vs private subnet

steps.text: The VPC internet gateway supports the public endpoint path.
The public subnet has an IGW route; the ALB has public reachability.
The ALB sends application traffic to a private IP target.
The instance has no direct IGW default route. Routing and filtering are independent.

scenarios.note: Subnets are AZ-scoped. A public route alone does not give every instance a usable public address.
scenarios.exam: SGs are stateful; NACLs are stateless. Check return-path rules for NACLs.

scenarios.title: 3 · Private outbound internet access

steps.text: The private instance starts an outbound connection.
Its default IPv4 route points to the public NAT in its AZ.
NAT translates traffic and uses its public-subnet IGW route.
Traffic reaches an external endpoint; return traffic follows the established path.

scenarios.note: The external client symbol represents an internet destination in this scenario. NAT does not admit unsolicited inbound requests.
scenarios.exam: For resilience, use per-AZ NAT routing where the design requires it; endpoints can avoid NAT for supported AWS services.

scenarios.title: 4 · ALB health checks / target routing

steps.text: ALB independently checks the configured path, port and success matcher.
Successful user traffic goes to eligible targets; a working homepage does not prove /health works.
Configured request logs expose client, target, status and timing evidence.

scenarios.note: An ALB request log, health-check evidence and aggregate metric answer different questions.
scenarios.exam: Inspect security groups, NACLs, path, port, matcher and application health.

scenarios.title: 5 · API Gateway → Lambda → DynamoDB

steps.text: Client calls the configured API endpoint.
Authorization, validation and integration settings permit a Lambda invoke.
Lambda runs with its execution-role permissions, distinct from the caller JWT.
Application code performs an authorized DynamoDB operation and checks record entitlement.

scenarios.note: This map uses a regional API endpoint; private and edge-optimized REST options have different connectivity.
scenarios.exam: API keys are for consumer usage plans, not authentication; an HTTP API does not have every REST feature.

scenarios.title: 6 · API Gateway prod / beta

steps.text: /prod/GetOrder or /beta/GetOrder selects the stage (custom-domain mappings can hide that name).
The stage points to an API deployment; stage variables can select configured backend aliases.
A production canary uses the same /prod URL, selecting the candidate deployment for a percentage.
Lambda alias/version selection is a separate object from the API deployment.

scenarios.note: Open the API Gateway card for the working prod/beta request, cache and usage-plan examples.
scenarios.exam: A deployment is an API snapshot; stage variables are configuration, not automatic body transformation.

scenarios.title: 7 · Cognito JWT authorization

steps.text: The user authenticates with the configured user pool or supported federated IdP.
Cognito issues tokens. The access token carries the scopes appropriate for API authorization.
The API authorizer validates the token and required access scope.
The backend is invoked; it still checks business/record authorization.

scenarios.note: Identity pools are a separate optional credential-brokering path when clients need direct AWS API access.
scenarios.exam: JWT validity does not imply AWS IAM permissions or entitlement to every record.

scenarios.title: 8 · SQS producer / consumer

steps.text: The producer sends a job; HTTP acceptance is not completion of the business operation.
Lambda event source mapping long-polls the queue.
A received batch becomes temporarily invisible.
The mapping invokes a Lambda worker with the batch.
The worker records an idempotent durable outcome.
After successful processing, the integration deletes acknowledged messages.

scenarios.note: Custom consumers explicitly call DeleteMessage themselves; Lambda mappings manage acknowledgement for successful work.
scenarios.exam: Visibility timeout ≠ retention; duplicate processing remains possible.

scenarios.title: 9 · SQS visibility / DLQ

steps.text: Receive the job; the visibility timeout starts.
Processing fails. The message is not successfully acknowledged.
After visibility expires, the job may be received again.
After the configured maximum receives, redrive sends it to the matching-type DLQ.

scenarios.note: This is a failing-job alternative to the successful queue scenario; the DLQ is not a broadcast subscription here.
scenarios.exam: Configure retries, idempotency, visibility extension and redrive deliberately.

scenarios.title: 10 · SNS fanout to queues

steps.text: Publish one event to an SNS topic.
A matching subscription delivers an independent copy to queue one.
Another subscription delivers an independent copy to queue two.
Each queue can have an independent consumer lifecycle.

scenarios.note: Each SQS subscription has its own independent retained copy and consumer lifecycle; filters can select which publications arrive.
scenarios.exam: Fanout copies delivery to subscribers; a competing-consumer queue divides work among its consumers.

scenarios.title: 11 · EventBridge routing

steps.text: Producer publishes an event to the selected event bus.
A rule pattern matches and delivers to its configured SQS target.
A consumer retrieves queued work independently.
The application processes the delivered job.

scenarios.note: Other supported targets and direct producer-to-queue publishing are alternatives.
scenarios.exam: EventBridge routes events; SQS buffers work. Rules do not turn a bus into a workflow state machine.

scenarios.title: 12 · Kinesis producer → shard → consumer

steps.text: A device creates a 4 KiB reading and sends PutRecord(s) over HTTPS.
Kinesis hashes its partition key into a shard range and assigns a sequence number.
The event source mapping polls the shard (or uses a configured enhanced-fan-out consumer).
Accepted records are returned in a batch; reads do not delete them.
Lambda processes the batch synchronously.
The worker writes an idempotent result to DynamoDB.

scenarios.note: Original stream records remain available until retention expires. At 4 KiB total per record, one sustained shard write budget is about 256 records/s.
scenarios.exam: A hot key can overload one shard while others are idle; inspect failed PutRecords entries even on HTTP 200.

scenarios.title: 13 · DynamoDB keys / GSI

steps.text: Write the item using its primary key, e.g. GameName + Version.
DynamoDB maintains a GSI for another query pattern such as Category + GameName.
Query the GSI and use an appropriate projection for the needed attributes.

scenarios.note: The index is an internal table feature, not a separate application hop or replacement database.
scenarios.exam: GSI reads are eventually consistent. An LSI uses the table partition key and is defined at table creation.

scenarios.title: 14 · DynamoDB Streams → Lambda

steps.text: Application changes an item.
The enabled stream emits a configured change record.
The event source mapping polls stream shards.
A change-record batch is returned.
The mapping invokes the processor; design downstream effects idempotently.

scenarios.note: Use a separate target or loop-prevention design if the processor writes back to its source table.
scenarios.exam: Stream consumption does not delete the source item. TTL removal happens asynchronously.

scenarios.title: 15 · RDS Multi-AZ failover

steps.text: The application uses the current primary endpoint.
Changes synchronously reach the traditional standby for availability.
After managed promotion, the application reconnects/retries against the writer endpoint.

scenarios.note: This demonstrates a Multi-AZ DB instance. A Multi-AZ DB cluster has two standby instances that can serve reads.
scenarios.exam: Traditional standby ≠ read replica; failover is not a guarantee that existing client connections survive.

scenarios.title: 16 · RDS read replica

steps.text: Send writes/strong-current operations to the primary.
Updates replicate asynchronously to the read replica.
The application explicitly routes lag-tolerant reads to the replica endpoint.

scenarios.note: An RDS read replica is distinct from an ElastiCache lookup and a traditional HA standby.
scenarios.exam: Replication lag affects read freshness; Multi-AZ alone is not always read scaling.

scenarios.title: 17 · EBS / EFS / S3

steps.text: EBS provides block storage attached to EC2 in the same AZ.
Another client uses its EFS mount target for shared files.
Both mount targets expose the same regional EFS filesystem.
An application uses object APIs for S3; no customer subnet hosts the bucket.

scenarios.note: These are alternative storage patterns, not a required chained write path.
scenarios.exam: Shared persistent cross-AZ files → regional EFS; same-AZ block device → EBS; objects → S3.

scenarios.title: 18 · Lambda versions / alias

steps.text: Clients/integrations invoke the stable alias.
The weighted alias selects an immutable published version, e.g. v1/v2.
CodeDeploy or an explicit alias update changes weights and supports rollback.

scenarios.note: The deployment step changes the route; it is not an extra HTTP hop for each invocation.
scenarios.exam: Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes environments; it is not the same as a weighted alias or reserved concurrency.

scenarios.title: 19 · Beanstalk rolling / immutable

steps.text: Rolling updates a batch of the existing fleet, temporarily reducing serving capacity.
Immutable is an alternative: validate a separate replacement fleet while retaining the original.
Health checks gate serving/release decisions.

scenarios.note: These steps compare alternatives; they are not sequential phases of a single deployment policy.
scenarios.exam: Rolling + additional batch preserves baseline capacity with a temporary batch. Persistent RDS should have an independent lifecycle.

scenarios.title: 20 · CDK / SAM → CloudFormation

steps.text: CDK constructs synthesize CloudFormation; CloudFormation does not synthesize CDK.
Alternatively, the SAM transform expands shorthand within a CloudFormation-compatible template.
CloudFormation provisions/updates the Lambda resource; Lambda later runs the code.
The same provisioning engine can manage EC2 and other supported resources.

scenarios.note: CDK and SAM are authoring choices, not a mandatory chain. SAM is explicit in current DVA-C02 Deployment skills.
scenarios.exam: AWS::Serverless::UserPool is invalid. Standard AWS::Cognito::UserPool can appear in a SAM template.

scenarios.title: 21 · Pipeline → build → deploy

steps.text: A versioned source revision starts the configured pipeline.
CodeBuild runs build/test/package commands.
For a container alternative, publish an immutable image artifact to ECR.
CodePipeline promotes the approved artifact through a deployment action.
CodeDeploy applies the configured rollout/rollback behavior to the target.

scenarios.note: CodeCommit is one source option; an ECR container artifact and a Lambda ZIP are alternative packaging choices.
scenarios.exam: Pipeline coordinates, Build executes build commands, Deploy promotes application revisions; runtime roles remain separate.

scenarios.title: 22 · IAM role assumption

steps.text: An authorized principal asks STS to assume the selected role.
The role trust policy allows that principal/federation relationship.
Temporary session credentials sign an allowed AWS operation; evaluate applicable resource policies too.
Organization guardrails can restrict the available action.

scenarios.note: The role in account B also illustrates the cross-account trust boundary; same-account roles use applicable trust/permission rules.
scenarios.exam: Trust and action permissions are separate. Boundaries/SCPs do not grant permissions.

scenarios.title: 23 · KMS envelope encryption

steps.text: The authorized application requests GenerateDataKey.
KMS returns a plaintext data key and a KMS-encrypted copy; underlying KMS key material stays protected.
The application encrypts data locally, stores ciphertext + encrypted data key and discards the plaintext data key.

scenarios.note: This illustrates client-side envelope encryption; S3 SSE-KMS is a different managed integration using KMS.
scenarios.exam: KMS directly handles small payloads; use a data key for large application data.

scenarios.title: 24 · Metrics / audit / tracing

steps.text: CloudWatch metrics/logs show operational behavior.
ALB access logs expose request-level details when configured.
X-Ray/OTel instrumentation correlates downstream request timing.
CloudTrail records configured AWS API activity, such as stack changes.
VPC Flow Logs describe IP flow metadata and filtering outcomes.

scenarios.note: These are parallel evidence sources, not a network service chain. CloudWatch also supports alarms, dashboards and custom metrics.
scenarios.exam: Choose logs for request details, metrics for trends, traces for timing, and CloudTrail for AWS API audit.

scenarios.title: 25 · Cross-account AWS access

steps.text: A supported external identity can federate only when the trust relationship and token claims are valid.
A caller using AWS credentials instead needs permission for AssumeRole.
Account B explicitly trusts the authorized principal; STS issues a role session.
The session performs only allowed actions; resource/key policies and applicable guardrails still apply.

scenarios.note: OIDC federation and a SigV4-signed AssumeRole request are alternative entry mechanisms, not the same request format.
scenarios.exam: Cross-account access needs both trust and permission; an external JWT does not automatically authorize AWS APIs.

comparisons.title: SQS vs Kinesis
comparisons.rule: SQS tracks pending jobs and deletes acknowledged messages. Kinesis retains ordered shard records for independent replay.
comparisons.exception: Both need duplicate-aware processing; receiving an SQS message merely hides it.

comparisons.title: SNS vs EventBridge
comparisons.rule: SNS fans publications to subscribers. EventBridge matches event-bus rules to targets.
comparisons.exception: Either can target SQS; a queue still owns the worker backlog.

comparisons.title: RDS Multi-AZ vs replica
comparisons.rule: Traditional Multi-AZ standby supports availability. A read replica serves explicitly routed reads with asynchronous lag.
comparisons.exception: Multi-AZ DB clusters are a separate model with readable standby instances.

comparisons.title: EBS vs EFS
comparisons.rule: EBS is same-AZ attached block storage. Regional EFS exposes shared files via AZ mount targets.
comparisons.exception: Supported EBS Multi-Attach is still same-AZ; EFS One Zone is not the regional model shown.

comparisons.title: ElastiCache vs DynamoDB
comparisons.rule: Cache reusable values with suitable expiry/invalidation versus durable key/document access patterns.
comparisons.exception: Memcached is not a durable primary datastore; Redis/Valkey durability options do not make it a relational SQL endpoint.

comparisons.title: Lambda vs EC2
comparisons.rule: Lambda handles supported invocations with managed execution. EC2 gives VM/OS control and fleet responsibilities.
comparisons.exception: Choose by execution, integration and control requirements, not by a blanket serverless preference.

comparisons.title: Security Groups vs NACLs
comparisons.rule: Security groups attach to ENIs and are stateful allow lists. NACLs associate with subnets and are stateless allow/deny lists.
comparisons.exception: Return traffic must satisfy NACL rules; these controls do not grant application or IAM entitlement.

comparisons.title: IAM role vs policy
comparisons.rule: A role is an assumable identity. A policy is a permission/trust document attached to the appropriate identity/resource.
comparisons.exception: Trust policy, identity permission policy, boundary and SCP have different responsibilities.

comparisons.title: CloudWatch vs CloudTrail
comparisons.rule: CloudWatch observes operations; CloudTrail audits configured AWS API/account events.
comparisons.exception: CloudWatch Logs can receive access/audit records, but destination does not change the meaning of the evidence.

comparisons.title: SAM vs CDK
comparisons.rule: SAM supplies serverless template shorthand and local tooling. CDK composes infrastructure in programming languages. Both use CloudFormation.
comparisons.exception: CDK can build serverless apps; SAM can include standard CloudFormation resources. Neither executes production code.

comparisons.title: Rolling vs Immutable
comparisons.rule: Rolling changes existing instances in batches. Immutable validates a replacement fleet while preserving the original.
comparisons.exception: Additional-batch rolling keeps baseline capacity but is not the same isolation model as immutable.

comparisons.title: Cognito user vs identity pools
comparisons.rule: User pools authenticate and issue JWTs. Identity pools exchange supported identities for scoped temporary AWS credentials.
comparisons.exception: Both can cooperate. A user-pool JWT is not itself a SigV4 credential.

study.title: Shared persistent files across AZs
study.answer: Choose regional EFS. EBS attachments remain in one AZ; S3 is object storage rather than a mounted POSIX filesystem.

study.title: Independent consumers need replay
study.answer: Choose a retained stream such as Kinesis. One SQS queue distributes acknowledged jobs; it does not provide the same independent retained log.

study.title: A serverless template, not a server
study.answer: SAM defines infrastructure; CloudFormation provisions it; Lambda executes supported function code.

study.title: Valid JWT; wrong tenant record
study.answer: Token validity is only one boundary. Enforce tenant/record entitlement in application/data access and scope caches appropriately.
